sections.title: Certifications: Lean Six Sigma belts

tips.title: Get credit for it
tips.highlight: There's a 1-unit elective where you can study for or earn a Green Belt for credit. Ask our major advisor, Richard Grotegut.
points: Tech 145 gives extra credit for a White Belt and MSI's Project Management Essentials Certification (Advanced).
Add any cert you finish to LinkedIn under Licenses & certifications. Most come with a badge you can show there too.

tips.title: What to get
points: Go for a Green Belt, not a Black Belt.
Tech 145 and Tech 31 already cover most of it (DMAIC, SIPOC, control charts, Gage R&R).
Want one before you graduate? IASSC has no prerequisites. One proctored exam, starts at $350 (check the current price and exam format).
Get the higher belts later through your job.

tips.title: Why not Black Belt?
points: Employers often expect a Black Belt to have led real improvement projects. Some certifications don't require that. Most students haven't led one.
Our professors say a new grad with one can look like a stretch. Plenty of engineers online agree.
It's not fake. It just doesn't mean much without projects behind it.

tips.title: Who gave you the belt matters
points: ASQ: the one quality people respect most, but you need 3 years of work experience first.
IASSC: open to students. Proctored, closed book, 70% to pass. Starts at $350.
MSI and other online ones: online exam plus a project simulation, no real project. Cheap, legit, but light.
Company programs with a real project count the most at that company.

tips.title: Going for the MSI Black Belt?
points: Our Tech 145 professor recommends it, and it's a fair path if you want to go deep on the tools.
Start with the White Belt for Tech 145 extra credit, then the MSI Black Belt online. It includes a project simulation, no real project needed.
The catch: it shows you passed the exam, not that you led a project. Some engineers will see a student Black Belt as a stretch.
So list it under your projects and experience, name MSI as the issuer, and have one real project ready to talk about.

tips.title: Already have one?
points: Keep it, but put it near the bottom of your resume, under your projects and experience.
List who issued it and the year.
Don't say you led a project if it was a simulation.
Have one real project ready to talk about. That's what they'll ask.

sections.intro: From our Tech 145 and Tech 190 professors, plus what engineers say online.

tips.title: Tech 31 + Tech 145 overlap
points: Same tools in both: DMAIC, SIPOC, CTQs, Gage R&R. Study them together.
Lean cuts waste. Six Sigma cuts defects and variation.

tips.title: Go on the tours
points: We toured Tesla and Rigetti this year. Best way to see a real line and meet engineers.
Talk to the engineers there. They can tell you about internships and what they look for when hiring.
Join a club project. Easy resume bullets before senior project.
